title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is analysing the 'équation des lacets' (the defining relations of pairs (λ,f) in what became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group). He pushes them through the 'reduction' of π̂_{0,3} and the orbifold groups at the elliptic points (i and ρ) into 2×2 matrices over Ẑ. This is in effect the image under π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1 → (P)SL(2,Ẑ), the congruence completion. The congruences ≡1 (2) on the next page confirm this reading.

Unknowns: two matrices g = (a b; c d) and f = (r s; t u) in SL(2,Ẑ), signs ε2, ε3 = ±1, and a multiplier μ ∈ Ẑ* (the cyclotomic-type character). Previous page: f ᵗf = (R S; T U) with R = r²+s², S = T = rt+su, U = t²+u².

Two norm forms appear. 1/μ = ε2(t²+u²) is the Gaussian norm, from the centraliser of the order-4 element. 1/μ = ε3(c²+cd+d²) is the Eisenstein norm, from the order-6 element.

This page:
(1) With c, d, r, s, t, u chosen, the remaining conditions det g = ε3 and C = ε2T (refs (61), (62)) form a linear system in (a,b):
 d a − c b = ε3,
 (c+d) a + d b = ε2ε3 S + (c²+cd+d²).
Its determinant is d² + c(c+d) = c²+cd+d² = 1/(με3), a unit of Ẑ. So (a,b) is uniquely determined: 'comme par hasard'.
(2) Reversing the viewpoint, start from μ. ε2 and ε3 are read off from congruences of μ, giving the representations 1/μ = ε2(t²+u²) = ε3(c²+cd+d²) with t, u, c, d ∈ Ẑ. Each of (t,u) and (c,d) 'depends on one parameter'. In modern terms the solution set is a torsor under the norm-one units of Ẑ[i], resp. Ẑ[ρ], i.e. Ẑ-points of a one-dimensional norm torus. Grothendieck wants an explicit parametrisation (parameters ε, σ, τ) but does not give it.
(3) Then r, s solve ur − ts = 1. These solutions form an affine line, cf. (87) on the previous page.
(4) The next page assembles everything: for fixed c, d, t, u the unknowns a, b, r, s satisfy a rank-3 affine-linear system, so the solutions form a 1-dimensional affine space over Ẑ.

In sum, the page describes, over Ẑ, the solution set of the matrix (congruence-level) shadow of the loop equations for a given multiplier μ.
errors: 'μ ≡ ε2 (2)' cannot be literally right: every unit of Ẑ is ≡ 1 mod 2. If t²+u² is a unit at 2, one of t, u is odd and the other even, so t²+u² ≡ 1 mod 4. The sign ε2 is therefore determined by μ mod 4, not mod 2. The mod-3 statement μ ≡ ε3 (3) is correct, since a unit c²+cd+d² is ≡ 1 mod 3.

Existence of the representations 1/μ = ε2 N(t+ui) = ε3 N(c+dρ) for every μ ∈ Ẑ* is asserted implicitly, not proved. It does hold by local norm surjectivity onto units at p ≠ 2 (resp. p ≠ 3), together with the mod-4 / mod-3 conditions at p = 2 (resp. p = 3).
The 'one parameter' description is left vague; Grothendieck himself says it 'faudrait dire' in a precise sense.
Equation label (88) duplicates the (88) used on the previous page.
I could not independently verify the derivation of the second equation from C = ε2T, because definitions (61)–(62) are not on this page. The determinant computation itself is correct.

ideas.what: Linear system for (a,b) whose determinant is the Eisenstein norm c²+cd+d², a unit, giving a unique solution
ideas.modern_name: elementary linear algebra over Ẑ; norm form of Z[ρ]

ideas.what: Writing 1/μ simultaneously as ±(Gaussian norm) and ±(Eisenstein norm) over Ẑ; signs read off from μ mod 4 and mod 3
ideas.modern_name: norms from Ẑ[i], Ẑ[ρ]; centralisers of the elliptic elements of SL2 (orders 4 and 6)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gauss/Eisenstein); local class field theory for norm surjectivity

ideas.what: Solution set of the matrix (congruence) shadow of the loop equations with fixed multiplier is a 1-dimensional affine space over Ẑ, fibred over norm-torus torsors
ideas.modern_name: image of GT-hat / Galois action in the congruence completion (P)SL2(Ẑ) of π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1, and of π_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: studied later in GT literature (Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, among others) in various forms; exact form unsure
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches GT-type objects; no such computation is published

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for an explicit parametrisation, with parameters ε, σ, τ, of the Ẑ-solutions of ε2(t²+u²) = ε3(c²+cd+d²) = 1/μ. He also wants the full description of matrix pairs (g,f) solving the congruence-level loop equations for a given μ. He leaves this unfinished.
missed.quote: les systèmes (t,u) comme (c,d) "dépendant de 1 paramètre", en un sens très concret qu'il faudrait dire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a concrete description of the possible images of GT-hat elements in SL2(Ẑ) via π_{0,3} → Γ(2). That could be compared with the known results that the Galois image there is governed by the cyclotomic character. It is likely recoverable from the existing literature, so the novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are elementary and correct apart from a mod 2 / mod 4 slip. Grothendieck's linearisation of the loop equations through SL2(Ẑ) with Gaussian and Eisenstein norm forms is a nice unpublished detail. But the congruence-level image of GT and Galois is fairly well understood, so this is unlikely to be new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The word written above '(t,u)', transcribed as '{+donc+}', looks more like 'discrets' or a similar insertion; uncertain.
'dans précisions qu'on y tenait' is probably 'si on y tenait' or 'dans la précision qu'on y tenait'.
The equation label is '(88)' (possibly '188)'), duplicating (88) on the previous page.
The crossed-out leading symbol in the second equation of (88) is a corrected 'c+d' (the original was likely 'a+d'); the transcription '(c+d)' is right.
